chapter_note: This is a substantial body↔cosmos microcosm teaching — classic correspondential substrate. The chapter is dominated by systematic mapping: head→firstfruit of garments, neck→ten firmaments, heart→sphere-wheel, thighs→air, etc.; then the watches and the four cosmoses of the body with seven archons each; then the twelve zodiacs mapped to body parts (whole-body and right/left halves). An apostolic dialogue frame opens it (4-6) and an Illuminator citation reintroduces the zodiac section (131). A hortatory-ascetic interlude (73-105) applies the body-cosmos correspondences to the elect — the cosmic mappings remain substratic but the addressee voice ("He who shall lord over X...") is application. Final section (179-197) on archonic powers in the body and disease shows some editorial drift but remains microcosmic teaching. Editorial fatigue score is mildly negative; substrate vocabulary dominant throughout; one seam flag at 76 around "elect."
